title: Hypergraph analysis of a text corpus
text: Three verbs complete analysis layer. hg_pagerank() ranks vertices stationary importance Chitra & Raphael (2019) random walk edge-dependent vertex weights – walk actually uses tf-idf weights (verified HyperNetX reference implementation machine precision): top-ranked abstracts corpus’s connective tissue – documents whose vocabulary reaches everywhere. personalized = vector turns verb “importance perspective documents”. dual_hypergraph() swaps vertex hyperedge roles fitted object, word-level view never requires re-tokenizing: Finally, hg_null_test() asks whether observed structure exceeds degree sequences alone imply: rewires binary membership degree-preserving checkerboard swaps (Gotelli 2000) compares. 2020 abstracts: Read two rows together: near-universal pairwise participation (0.988) evidence structure – null reproduces (p = 0.36), vocabulary-rich abstracts connect everything degree-preserving rewiring. mean edge Jaccard significant (z = 2.48, p = 0.01): words repeat ’s document combinations frequencies require, exactly topical co-occurrence clustering exploits. decisive practice: never report structural statistic without null interval.

code: library(hypernets)  # memory network: what follows what, given how you got here hon <- build_hon(human_long, action = "code", actor = "session_id",                  time = "timestamp", max_order = 3) hon_centrality(hon, sort_by = "pagerank")  # simplicial complex: the same sessions as a pathway complex sc <- build_simplicial(hon, type = "pathway") betti_numbers(sc)  # hypergraph: each session as one multi-way interaction over its codes hg <- group_hypergraph(human_long, actor = "code", group = "session_id") hypergraph_centrality(hg, type = "pagerank")  # text: a corpus as a document-word hypergraph, clustered into topics thg <- text_hypergraph(covid_abstracts, column = "abstract", id = "doc",                        weight = "tfidf", stop_words = stop_words_en(),                        min_count = 3L) topics <- hg_cluster(thg, k = 4, type = "random_walk", seed = 1) hg_keywords(thg, topics, n = 5, collapse = TRUE)                    # tf-idf mass hg_keywords(thg, topics, n = 5, type = "ctfidf", collapse = TRUE)  # BERTopic's c-TF-IDF hg_keywords(thg, topics, n = 5, type = "centrality", collapse = TRUE)

what: Bottleneck Distance Between Persistence Diagrams — bottleneck_distance
title: Bottleneck Distance Between Persistence Diagrams — bottleneck_distance
text: Computes bottleneck distance two persistence diagrams. finite pairs, bottleneck distance $$W_\infty(D_1, D_2) = \inf_{\gamma} \sup_{p \D_1} \|p - \gamma(p)\|_\infty,$$ \(\gamma\) ranges bijections \(D_1 \cup \Delta \D_2 \cup \Delta\) \(\Delta = \{(x,x)\}\) diagonal. point may match point diagram projection onto diagonal cost \(|d - b|/2\). Computed via binary search \(\varepsilon\) plus Kuhn bipartite-matching feasibility check. Essential classes (death = Inf VR mode, death = 0 clique mode) matched one--one within dimension. diagrams different numbers essential classes dimension, bottleneck distance dimension Inf.

Directed inputs symmetrised underlying clique enumerator. p Probability [0, 1] k-clique k >= 3 becomes k-hyperedge. Default 1 (deterministic - every found clique included). type Hyperedge enumeration. "clique" (default) promotes k-cliques binarised adjacency k-hyperedges. metric Vietoris-Rips construction implemented; "vr" / "rips" accepted match.arg raise error rather silently aliasing "clique". include_pairwise Logical. Include 2-edges input network 2-hyperedges. Default TRUE. Set FALSE "fully higher-order" hypergraph containing k-hyperedges k >= 3. max_size Integer >= 2. Maximum hyperedge size extract. Default 3L (triangles ). 4L also includes 4-cliques 4-hyperedges, etc. threshold Numeric. Edge weight cutoff used binarise adjacency clique enumeration. Default 0 (non-zero weight edge). seed Optional integer reproducible Bernoulli sampling 0 < p < 1. x net_hypergraph object (print). ... Additional arguments (ignored). object net_hypergraph object (summary).

title: Higher-order hypergraph from a network's clique structure — build_hypergraph
text: net_hypergraph object: list components hyperedges List integer vectors. entry hyperedge given sorted node indices spans. incidence Numeric matrix size n_nodes x n_hyperedges. incidence[, j] = 1 iff node belongs hyperedge j. Row names node names; column names h1, h2, ... nodes Character vector node names. n_nodes, n_hyperedges Scalar counts. size_distribution Named integer vector: number hyperedges size, named size_2, size_3, ... params Recorded call parameters: source, type, p, include_pairwise, max_size, threshold, seed. input x invisibly. data.frame, one row per node: node, degree (number hyperedges node belongs ). Returned invisibly: summary(x) prints summary nothing else; assign result keep table.

title: Higher-order hypergraph from a network's clique structure — build_hypergraph
text: construction follows Burgio, Matamalas, Gomez & Arenas (2020) simplicial / hypergraph contagion. k-clique k >= 3 found underlying graph (via build_simplicial()), independent Bernoulli(p) trial decides whether clique becomes k-hyperedge. Underlying pairwise edges always retained include_pairwise = TRUE, resulting hypergraph contains original 2-edge structure sampled higher-order interactions. limits: p = 0 include_pairwise = TRUE reproduces input pairwise network hypergraph size-2 edges. p = 1 include_pairwise = FALSE returns fully higher-order hypergraph containing k-hyperedges (k >= 3) found network's clique complex.

title: Higher-order hypergraph from a network's clique structure — build_hypergraph
text: Burgio, G., Matamalas, J. T., Gomez, S., & Arenas, . (2020). Evolution cooperation presence higher-order interactions: networks hypergraphs. Entropy 22(7), 744. doi:10.3390/e22070744

title: Higher-order hypergraph from a network's clique structure — build_hypergraph
code: set.seed(1) n <- 8 adj <- matrix(stats::rbinom(n * n, 1, 0.5), n, n) diag(adj) <- 0 adj <- (adj + t(adj)) > 0 rownames(adj) <- colnames(adj) <- LETTERS[seq_len(n)] hg <- build_hypergraph(adj, p = 1, max_size = 3L) print(hg) #> Hypergraph: 8 nodes, 51 hyperedges #> Size distribution: #>   size_2   : 23 #>   size_3   : 28 #> Source: network cliques (p = 1.00, include_pairwise = TRUE, max_size = 3) summary(hg) #> Hypergraph summary #>   Nodes:         8 #>   Hyperedges:    51 #>   Mean size:     2.55 #>   Max size:      3

title: Build a Simplicial Complex — build_simplicial
text: Constructs simplicial complex network higher-order pathway object. Two construction methods available: Clique complex ("clique"): every clique thresholded non-zero graph becomes simplex. Edges absolute weight \(\geq\) threshold retained. standard bridge graph theory algebraic topology. Pathway complex ("pathway"): higher-order pathway net_hon net_hypa becomes simplex. type = "vr" (alias "rips"), input treated non-negative distance / dissimilarity matrix Vietoris-Rips filtration constructed: k-simplex \(\sigma\) enters \(\max_{(,j) \\sigma} d(,j)\). Use max_scale cap filtration diameter; edges d(,j) > max_scale excluded. Filtration values attached $filtration returned object persistent_homology() can read directly.

title: Build a Simplicial Complex — build_simplicial
code: build_simplicial(   x,   type = "clique",   threshold = 0,   max_dim = 10L,   max_pathways = NULL,   anomaly = c("all", "over", "under"),   max_scale = NULL,   ... )

title: Build a Simplicial Complex — build_simplicial
text: x square matrix, tna, netobject, net_hon, net_hypa, net_mogen. type Construction type: "clique" (default), "pathway", "vr" (alias "rips"). threshold type = "clique": minimum non-zero absolute edge weight include edge (default 0). Edges ignored; zero-weight non-edges never included. Ignored type = "vr" - use max_scale instead. max_dim Maximum simplex dimension (default 10). Must single non-negative integer. k-simplex k+1 nodes. max_pathways type = "pathway": maximum number pathways include, ranked count (HON) ratio (HYPA). NULL includes . Default NULL. anomaly HYPA pathway complexes, anomaly direction include: "" (default), "", "". -represented HYPA paths ranked smallest observed/expected ratio; -represented paths ranked largest ratio. max_scale type = "vr": maximum edge length include filtration. NULL (default) uses max(d). ... Additional arguments passed build_hon() x tna/netobject type = "pathway".

title: Build a Simplicial Complex — build_simplicial
code: mat <- matrix(c(0,.6,.5,.6,0,.4,.5,.4,0), 3, 3) colnames(mat) <- rownames(mat) <- c("A","B","C") sc <- build_simplicial(mat, threshold = 0.3) print(sc) #> Clique Complex  #>   3 nodes, 7 simplices, dimension 2 #>   Density: 100.0%  |  Mean dim: 0.71  |  Euler: 1 #>   f-vector: (f0=3 f1=3 f2=1) #>   Betti: b0=1 #>   Nodes: A, B, C  betti_numbers(sc) #> b0 b1 b2  #>  1  0  0   # Vietoris-Rips on a distance matrix: d <- 1 - mat diag(d) <- 0 sc_vr <- build_simplicial(d, type = "vr", max_scale = 0.6)

text: x character vector, data.frame text column. column x data.frame, name text column. html Decode HTML entities (&,  , ’, ...) strip tags (default TRUE). encoding Repair common UTF-8-read--Latin-1 mojibake (three-character garble curly apostrophe) normalise typographic quotes, dashes non-breaking spaces ASCII forms (default TRUE). citations Remove bracketed reference numbers ([12], [3, 4], [1-5]), leading list markers (1., (3), )) dotted section numbers (3.2.1) (default TRUE). urls Remove URLs, www. addresses, doi: strings bare DOIs (default TRUE). copyright Remove trailing copyright notice: everything last copyright sign, (c) Copyright end tail copyright_max characters, plus "rights reserved" (default TRUE). copyright_max Longest tail treated notice (default 300). numbers Remove bare numbers, percentages years (default TRUE). Default NULL. stop_words Words remove, case-insensitively word boundaries (default NULL, none). Usually left text_hypergraph()'s stop_words; use cleaned text shown. min_content Minimum share alphabetic characters among non-space characters, judged repaired text numbers removed (default 0, keep everything). reference list table fragment scores low; 0.5 sensible floor abstracts.

title: Clique expansion of a hypergraph — clique_expansion
text: clique expansion standard "loss-y lossless--pairwise" projection: preserves pairs co-occurred often discards higher-order grouping. Comparing clique_expansion(hg) directly-estimated pairwise network (e.g. via Nestimate::cooccurrence() data) quantifies much information carried hyperedge structure. Computed one BLAS call via tcrossprod(incidence); runs O(n_nodes^2 * n_hyperedges) time, fast typical sizes. Closes /O cycle: event data -> group_hypergraph() -> clique_expansion() -> function accepts netobject (centrality, bootstrap, clustering, plotting via cograph).

Several allowed. method null. "swap" (default) checkerboard swap chain : margins preserved exactly, vertex may repeat within hyperedge. "configuration" draws independent stub-matchings (Chodrow 2020), standard higher-order configuration model: vertex stubs matched uniformly random hyperedge slots, margins hold collapse (vertex whose stubs land twice one hyperedge loses degree). "assignment" degree-ordered assignment Coupette et al. title: Higher-order centralities with first-order projection — hon_centrality
text: hon net_hon object build_hon(). type Character vector, subset c("pagerank", "betweenness", "closeness"). Default computes three. project Logical. TRUE (default) returns one row per first-order state; FALSE returns one row per higher-order node ordinary directed-graph centralities higher-order topology (useful see contexts, states, dominate). projection higher-order node's PageRank distributed states path project = TRUE: "scaled" (default, pathpy's default - k states receives k-th value, projected PageRank still sums 1), "last" (state actually occupied), "first", "" (every state path receives full value; result longer sums 1). Ignored betweenness closeness, first-order construction. damping PageRank damping factor (0, 1). Default 0.85. weighted Logical. FALSE (default, pathpy's convention) runs PageRank binary higher-order topology; TRUE uses edge weights hon$matrix. max_iter, tol Power-iteration controls PageRank. max_paths Integer cap shortest paths enumerated betweenness. Exceeding raises hypernets_too_many_paths error rather silently truncating. Default 1e6. sort_by NULL (alphabetical state node, default) one requested types - sort table centrality, largest first, ties broken state/node order stays deterministic. top Integer NULL. Return first top rows, applied filter sort_by, sort_by top compose. Default NULL returns every row.

title: Hypergraph eigenvector centralities — hypergraph_centrality
text:
Clique-motif eigenvector centrality (CEC): forms clique-expanded pairwise graph \(W\) \(W_{ij} = |\{e : , j \e\}|\) returns leading eigenvector \(W\). Equivalent running igraph::eigen_centrality() clique_expansion() output. Z-eigenvector centrality (ZEC): solves linear eigen-equation hyperedge tensor, $$\lambda\, x_i \;=\; \sum_{e 
i }\; \prod_{j \e,\; j 
eq } x_j,$$ via power iteration. Works hypergraphs mixed edge sizes. H-eigenvector centrality (HEC): solves power-k-1 eigen-equation, $$\lambda\, x_i^{k-1} \;=\; \sum_{e 
i }\; \prod_{j \e,\; j 
eq } x_j.$$ uniform hypergraphs (hyperedges size \(k\)), equivalent normalizing ZEC update geometric-mean exponent \(1/(k-1)\). mixed sizes, effective exponent taken largest hyperedge; expect slightly different rankings ZEC mixed case. Hypergraph PageRank ("pagerank"): stationary distribution damped EDVW random walk Chitra & Raphael (2019): node \(v\), pick hyperedge \(e 
i v\) probability proportional weight \(w(e)\), node \(u \e\) probability proportional edge-dependent vertex weight \(\gamma_e(u)\) (incidence cell, .e. occurrence totals window_hypergraph()); probability \(1 - damping\) teleport uniformly. collapse theorem: edge-independent vertex weights (binary incidence) walk equivalent PageRank weighted clique expansion edge weights \(\sum_{e 
i u,v} w(e)/\delta(e)\) – hypergraph adds information exactly \(\gamma\) edge-dependent. Nodes left hyperedge (possible min_weight/min_size filtering) teleport every step receive teleportation mass. undamped stationary distribution walk pi column reported hypergraph_cluster(). Subhypergraph centrality ("subhypergraph"): logarithm diagonal matrix exponential clique adjacency derived binary incidence (entries count shared hyperedges), \(\log[\exp(W)]_{ii}\). counts closed walks based node factorial penalty length matches implementation used HypergraphX 1.5 legal-hypergraphs analysis.

Diagonal zero. Hyperedge-level (length n_hyperedges m x m)  edge_sizes Hyperedge sizes \(|e|\). edge_pairwise_overlap m x m matrix: |e_i intersect e_j|. Global (scalars)  density k-uniform hypergraphs: m / choose(n, k). mixed sizes: sum(|e|) / (n * m) (mean fraction nodes per hyperedge). avg_edge_size Mean edge_sizes. size_distribution Tabulation hyperedge sizes (passed hg). intersection_profile Distribution pairwise hyperedge intersection sizes - useful spotting whether hyperedges overlap mostly trivially share substantial cores (et al. 2020). pairwise_participation Fraction node pairs co-appearing least one hyperedge. n_nodes, n_hyperedges Convenience scalars. input x invisibly.

title: Structural measures for a hypergraph — hypergraph_measures
text: measures computed via standard matrix operations binary incidence \(B = (b_{ij})\) \(b_{ij} = 1\) iff node \(\) hyperedge \(j\): hyperdegree = rowSums(B), edge_sizes = colSums(B) co_degree = tcrossprod(B) (zero diagonal) edge_pairwise_overlap = crossprod(B) (zero diagonal) overlap_coefficient[, j] = overlap[, j] / min(edge_sizes[], edge_sizes[j]) jaccard[, j] = overlap[, j] / (edge_sizes[] + edge_sizes[j] - overlap[, j]) Empty hypergraph (n_hyperedges == 0) returns trivial zeros empty matrices.

what: Test the Markov order of a sequential process — markov_order_test
title: Test the Markov order of a sequential process — markov_order_test
text: Principled test whether categorical sequence best described \(k\)-th order Markov chain. order \(k = 1, \ldots,\) max_order, function computes classical likelihood-ratio statistic (\(G^2\)) conditional independence \(s \perp x \mid w\), \(w\) \((k-1)\)-gram context, \(x\) extra (k-th-back) state added order \(k\), \(s\) next state. \(H_0\) (order-\((k-1)\) correct), \(s\) independent \(x\) given \(w\). null distribution obtained exact within-\(w\) permutation test: context \(w\) successor labels exchangeable \(H_0\), shuffling \(s\) within \(w\)-group yields exact reference distribution \(G^2\). plug-MLE bias refitting per replicate. asymptotic \(\chi^2\) p-value reported alongside reference. optimal order smallest \(k\) significantly better \(k - 1\) level alpha: keep raising order test rejects, stop first non-rejection.

title: Persistent Homology — persistent_homology
text: Computes persistent homology via full boundary-matrix reduction \(\mathbb{Z}/2\) (Edelsbrunner, Letscher & Zomorodian 2000). returned persistence diagram pairs k-dimensional homology class simplex whose addition creates (birth) simplex whose addition destroys (death). Essential classes - never killed - reported death = 0 clique mode (similarity scale, descending) death = Inf VR mode (distance scale, ascending). Two filtration modes supported: type = "clique" Weighted clique filtration. Input treated similarity matrix; high-weight simplices appear early. k-simplex \(\sigma\), filtration value \(\min_{(,j) \\sigma}\,|w(,j)|\). Thresholds run high low. type = "vr" Vietoris-Rips filtration non-negative distance matrix. k-simplex \(\sigma\), filtration value \(\max_{(,j) \\sigma}\,d(,j)\). Thresholds run low high. Use max_scale cap filtration diameter.
